thread:
raj_acme: Hey team — hitting a wall onboarding SSO+SCIM for our trial org. SAML login works, but SCIM provisioning calls from Okta to /scim/v2/Users return 403.
elaine: Hi Raj — sorry you're blocked. Can you paste the exact endpoint and header you're using?
raj_acme: Using https://api.redwood-inference.com/orgs/ACME123/scim/v2/Users, header Authorization: Bearer <token-redacted>. Okta logs show 403 from target.
sam_b: 403 usually token/role issue. For hosted POCs we issue a SCIM service token tied to the trial org and a minimal ACL. Did you check the token in the Account > Integrations screen?
raj_acme: I have a token listed but not sure if it's SCIM-enabled. Where is that set?
elaine: I can repro with a curl test — try this and paste the output (redact token):

```
curl -i -X GET
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <SCIM_TOKEN>"
  -H "Accept: application/scim+json"
  "https://api.redwood-inference.com/orgs/ACME123/scim/v2/Users"
```

mo: Also confirm Okta is sending userName/email as the SCIM identifier. Our SCIM implementation expects userName to be the canonical username (usually email). If Okta is mapping a different attribute, we return 403 for duplicate/invalid mapping in some cases.
raj_acme: Okta is mapping userName -> user.email.
elaine: If curl above returns 403, include response body. Common causes: 1) token expired/rotated, 2) token scoped to a different org, 3) org-level SCIM disabled, 4) request origin IP blocked for Dedicated/private setups.
sam_b: Quick checks:
- Confirm token in Account > SCIM tokens matches what Okta is using.
- In Okta SCIM app, set Base URL exactly to https://api.redwood-inference.com/orgs/ACME123/scim/v2
- Ensure Authorization header is "Bearer <token>" (no extra quotes).
- Retry with curl to isolate Okta from network issues.

raj_acme: Curl shows: HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 16:44:08 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "insufficient_scope",
  "message": "SCIM provisioning not enabled for token or org mismatch"
}

mo: That message is explicit — token-org mismatch or not SCIM-enabled. Elaine — can you check the token metadata server-side?
elaine: On it. raj_acme — I'm going to create a temporary SCIM token and paste into Okta. Expect a short maintenance window.
onboarding-bot: Created temporary SCIM token for org ACME123, expires in 24h. Token ID: tk_tmp_8f7c. (token value delivered via secure DM) :white_check_mark:
katie: Quick Q from a procurement perspective — if we flip this to Dedicated for POC (reserved pool), will we still use the same SCIM endpoint or is there an IP allowlist step?
mo: Good question. Hosted POC uses api.redwood-inference.com (no IP allowlist). Dedicated/Private deployments require either: 1) VPC peering settings + allowlisted Okta IPs, or 2) a customer-owned ingress. We'll send a short checklist.
elaine: raj_acme — after I rotate token, do one sync and let me know status. If still 403, we'll check token metadata and org binding. If 200, then you can enable push provisioning in Okta.
raj_acme: Got the token via DM, updating Okta now...
(6 minutes)
raj_acme: Okta test user sync succeeded. Users provisioned. Thanks! :tada:
elaine: Great. Follow-ups:
- We'll add a note in the trial onboarding doc about SCIM token binding and example curl.
- mo to send Dedicated/Private SCIM network checklist to raj_acme and katie.
mo: Sending checklist now (will include IP ranges, hostnames, and expected headers).
elaine: Also looping in Security for a quick Q: can we support rotating SCIM tokens automatically via the API for customers? (separate convo).

idp-bot: Note: SAML metadata uploaded for ACME123 at 2026-02-17T16:52:00Z.
katie: Back to pricing — Raj, if you want a short Dedicated trial, I can put together a 30-day reserved quote that includes support for private provisioning.
raj_acme: Appreciated. For now hosted flow is fine. Will reach out if we need Dedicated. Thanks everyone!
elaine: Closing loop — marking onboarding as resolved, adding a short KB with the curl snippet and 'common 403 causes'. :white_check_mark:
